questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make a complaint by phone
Why call centres have long queues
The growing use of AI in call centres and its effect on workers
How to get a job in a call centre
questions.why: They ask who's really in charge at the call centre: humans or AI.

questions.q: How does Phil feel when his call is put on hold?
options: Usually frustrated, but he likes knowing his place in the queue
Relaxed, because he enjoys listening to the music while he waits
Angry, so he always hangs up
He doesn't mind at all
questions.why: He's usually frustrated, but likes it when a number says how many people are in front.

questions.q: Why is AI causing problems in countries like India and the Philippines?
options: Their phone networks are too slow
Customers there don't trust AI
AI doesn't understand the local languages spoken in those countries
Call centre jobs are a big part of their economies
questions.why: Pippa says call centre jobs make up a big part of the economy there.

options: A computer programmer who builds AI systems for call centres
The president of a union for call centre workers
A manager at a big call centre
A customer who complained about AI
questions.why: She is president of the call centre workers' union, B.I.E.N.

options: She has to work at night
She has to speak many different languages with customers every day
She has to travel a lot
She calms angry, shouting customers while AI monitors her
questions.why: She must pacify yelling clients, and 'you're being monitored by an AI'.

questions.q: Why does Mylene mention a study?
options: To show that AI creates new jobs
To support her fear that AI will replace many workers
To prove that customers much prefer talking to humans than to AI
To explain how AI monitors calls
questions.why: She cites a study saying about 27% of workers will be displaced by AI.

questions.q: Why does Mylene believe AI will never fully replace humans?
options: Because AI lacks empathy
Because AI is too expensive
Because AI makes too many mistakes
Because the law protects workers
questions.why: She says she doesn't think AI is empathetic, and people are more compassionate.

questions.q: What does Pippa point out about the way Mylene speaks?
options: She speaks very fast
She uses lots of technical words that listeners may not understand
She often says 'you know' to give herself time to think
She never pauses
questions.why: Pippa says Mylene says 'you know' a lot – a filler that gives the speaker time to think.
